catalog.chrome: Google Chrome web browser. Uses one process per tab, extension and GPU task.
catalog.webview2: Embedded browser engine used by other Windows apps to display web content.
catalog.safari: Safari web browser and WebKit page renderers.
catalog.vscode: Visual Studio Code editor, including its extension host and language servers.
catalog.cursor: Cursor AI code editor (VS Code based).
catalog.visualstudio: Microsoft Visual Studio IDE and its build/background services.
catalog.jetbrains: JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm…). Indexing can use lots of CPU and RAM.
catalog.docker: Docker Desktop and its container engine.
catalog.vmmem: Memory and CPU of the WSL2 / Hyper-V virtual machine (often Docker). Ending it shuts the VM down.
catalog.ollama: Ollama local AI model runner. Large models use a lot of RAM and GPU.
catalog.steam: Steam game store, launcher and its embedded web views.
catalog.riot: Riot Games client and Vanguard anti-cheat.
catalog.nvidia: NVIDIA driver services, overlay and recording tools.
catalog.adobecc: Adobe Creative Cloud background sync, licensing and update services.
catalog.figma: Figma design tool and its local font agent.
catalog.gdrive: Google Drive for desktop file sync.
catalog.svchost: Windows service host: runs one or more system services. Stop the service, not the host.
catalog.explorer: Windows desktop, taskbar and File Explorer. Ending it hides the taskbar until it restarts.
catalog.dwm: Desktop Window Manager: draws every window on screen.
catalog.searchindexer: File search indexer. Heavy CPU/disk use is temporary while it catalogues new files.
catalog.defender: Antivirus real-time protection. Protected by the OS.
catalog.wmiprvse: WMI provider host: answers system queries from other programs (monitoring tools, drivers).
catalog.tiworker: Windows Update installer. Ending it can interrupt an update in progress.
catalog.runtimebroker: Checks permissions for Windows Store apps.
catalog.windowserver: macOS display server: draws every window on screen.
catalog.launchd: macOS init system: starts and supervises every other process.
catalog.systemd: Linux init system and service manager.
catalog.displayserver: Linux display server or desktop shell.

cleaner.title: Deep cleanup
cleaner.recoverable: Up to {{size}} can be reclaimed. Review what each item does before cleaning.
cleaner.preserved: Never touched: your documents, passwords, bookmarks, extensions, browser settings and installed programs.
cleaner.notElevatedWin: RePID is not running as administrator, so system-level items (Windows temp, update cache) will be skipped.
cleaner.notElevatedUnix: System-level items will ask for your password once when you clean.

unavailable.not-found: Nothing to clean here right now.
unavailable.needs-full-disk-access: macOS blocks access. Grant RePID "Full Disk Access" in System Settings → Privacy & Security, then scan again.
unavailable.unsupported: Not available on this operating system.

cleaner.blockedBy: {{names}} is open. It must close to clean this — you will be asked first.
cleaner.needsAdminNote: Will be skipped without administrator rights.

status.partial: Partly cleaned · {{size}} freed · {{skipped}} in use or protected
status.skipped-running: Skipped: the app was still open

user-temp.title: Temporary files & user caches
user-temp.effect: Deletes temporary files, crash reports and thumbnail/shader caches. Apps recreate them when needed; the first launch of some games or apps may be a little slower. Files currently in use are skipped.

system-temp.title: System temporary files
system-temp.effect: Deletes system-wide temporary files and old error reports. Your documents are not affected; files in use are skipped. Needs administrator rights.

update-cache.title: Update download cache
update-cache.effect: Deletes already-downloaded update installers. Installed updates are NOT removed; if an update is still pending, the system will download it again.

recycle-bin.title: Recycle Bin / Trash
recycle-bin.effect: PERMANENTLY deletes everything in the recycle bin. This cannot be undone and the files cannot be recovered.

dns-cache.title: DNS cache
dns-cache.effect: Flushes cached domain-name lookups. Helps when a site fails to load after a network change. No downside: the next visits simply resolve names again.

dev-caches.title: Package manager caches (npm, Yarn, pip)
dev-caches.effect: Deletes downloaded package caches. Your projects are untouched, but the next install will download packages again (slower and needs internet).

browser-cache.title: Cache
browser-cache.effect: Deletes images, scripts and files saved from websites. Pages load a little slower the first time. You stay signed in and passwords are kept.

browser-history.title: Browsing history
browser-history.effect: Deletes visited pages, address-bar suggestions, most-visited tiles and the tabs saved for "restore session". Cannot be undone. Bookmarks and passwords are kept.

browser-cookies.title: Cookies & sign-ins
browser-cookies.effect: Signs you out of EVERY website (email, social networks, banking) and erases site preferences. You will need to sign in again and may have to repeat two-step verification.

confirm.sensitiveAck: I understand the consequences and want to continue.
confirm.closeBlockingHint: Unsaved work in those windows (open forms, downloads in progress) will be lost. If unchecked, their items are skipped.

startup.title: Startup programs
startup.scanning: Checking what opens when the computer starts…
startup.summary: {{enabled}} open on their own at sign-in · {{mem}} in use right now
startup.safeNote: Disabling never uninstalls or deletes anything: the program just stops opening automatically at sign-in. You can turn it back on here any time.
startup.nextBoot: Takes effect at your next sign-in. Apps that are already open stay open.
startup.notElevatedWin: Some programs are registered for every user of this computer; changing them requires administrator rights.
startup.unsupported: Startup management is not available on this platform.
startup.whatHappens: What happens if you disable it:
startup.suggestedHint: Rarely needed at startup and safe to disable.
startup.lockedHint: Operating-system component or locked by policy: RePID will not disable it.
startup.adminHint: Registered for all users: requires administrator rights.
startup.impactHint: Measured now from what it uses while open.

effect.updater: It will check for updates when you open the program instead of sitting in the background from boot.
effect.browser: The browser (or web app) won't preload at sign-in; the first time you open it may take a couple of seconds longer.
effect.communication: You won't get messages or calls from this app until you open it yourself.
effect.media: The app won't open on its own. Your music, library and settings stay intact.
effect.gaming: The launcher won't open on its own. Your games stay installed; downloads and updates start when you open it.
effect.cloud: Your files stop syncing until you open the app: anything you change meanwhile won't be backed up to the cloud.
effect.security: It may stop alerting you or protecting in real time whatever this product watches. Only do this if you know you don't need it.
effect.hardware: Hardware features that rely on this utility may stop working: special keys, audio controls, lighting, advanced touchpad, or camera and microphone effects.
effect.development: Developer tools (containers, local servers) won't be ready until you open them.
effect.system: It is part of the operating system and stays enabled.
effect.generic: The program won't open automatically; you can open it yourself whenever you need it.

confirm.title: Disable at startup
confirm.body: These programs will stop opening automatically at sign-in. Nothing is uninstalled or deleted.
confirm.cautionAck: I understand what will happen and want to disable them anyway.

boost.title: Performance mode
boost.inactive: Off · pick a profile to prioritize what you're doing
boost.safeNote: No app is closed and nothing is deleted. The selected apps keep working; they just yield CPU to what you're using. Everything goes back to normal when you press “Restore all”, close RePID, or restart the app.

gaming.title: Gaming
gaming.desc: Priority to your game. Browsers, sync and updaters yield CPU. Voice chat, overlays and launchers are left alone.

work.title: Focus
work.desc: Game launchers and background processes yield CPU to your work apps.

creative.title: Render / build
creative.desc: Everything non-essential yields CPU to your editor, renderer or build.

custom.title: Custom
custom.desc: You choose which apps to adjust; nothing is pre-selected.

focus.label: Priority app
focus.hint: Gets above-normal priority. “High” and “Realtime” are never used: they can freeze keyboard and audio.
focus.unsupported: On macOS and Linux raising priority requires root; RePID only lowers the other apps.

boost.listHint: Pre-selected by the profile. You can change the selection.
boost.ecoEffect: It keeps working normally; when the computer is busy it waits its turn and may respond a little slower while the mode is on.
boost.ecoQosNote: On Windows 11 it also turns on “Efficiency mode” (the green leaf in Task Manager).
boost.protectedCount_one: {{count}} system, service or security app is left alone.
boost.protectedCount_other: {{count}} system, service and security apps are left alone.
boost.empty: No background app is using a meaningful amount of resources right now.
boost.notRunning: Closed · will be adjusted if you open it again
boost.restorePending: Some priorities could not be restored because the password prompt was cancelled. They return to normal when those apps restart.
boost.detailHint: Lowers its priority without closing it. Restored when you turn it off or close RePID.
boost.detailBlocked: System apps, services, security software and apps marked caution keep their priority.

toast.stopped: All restored: apps are back to their original priority
